title: Unemployment Benefit Claims — Rule on Holding Several Claims and One Open Claim per Program
content:
**1.** A claimant may hold several Unemployment Benefit Claims records over time and may hold claims under different programs at once, so the number of claim records per claimant is not capped.

**2.** A new claim under a program may be filed only when the claimant holds no other claim under the same program whose status is filed, active, on hold, inactive or exhausted. At most 1 open claim per program is held at a time.

**3.** A claim under the same program whose status is closed, withdrawn or ineligible does not block a new filing, and a claim filed after a benefit year ends starts a new benefit year with a new base period.

**4.** Whether claims under different programs may be filed and paid together is decided by the Department's program sequencing rules.

## Basis of the filing condition

The condition in clause 2 is read from the claim records, before the new claim is filed. It compares the claimant and the program of the new claim with the claimant's existing claim records under that same program; a claim under a different program is not counted under clause 2.

| Status of the claimant's existing claim under the same program | Effect on a new filing under that program |
|---|---|
| Filed | Blocks the new filing |
| Active | Blocks the new filing |
| On hold | Blocks the new filing |
| Inactive | Blocks the new filing |
| Exhausted | Blocks the new filing |
| Closed | Does not block |
| Withdrawn | Does not block |
| Ineligible | Does not block |

### Hypothetical cases

- A claimant whose Regular State Unemployment Insurance claim stands exhausted asks to file another Regular State Unemployment Insurance claim: the exhausted claim blocks the filing under clause 2.
- The same claimant's earlier Regular State Unemployment Insurance claim stands closed at the end of its benefit year: it does not block, and the new claim starts a new benefit year with a new base period under clause 3.
